scientific_question: How much of the Guánica–Mona difference in realized reproduction can be accounted for by visitor abundance/composition after weighting each visitor by direct per-visit effectiveness, without confusing a stable self/outcross breeding-system index with stable total reproduction?

known_source_native_structure.guanica: higher visitation and extreme Apis mellifera dominance
known_source_native_structure.mona: lower visitation, higher visitor richness and much more even assemblage
known_source_native_structure.autogamy: negligible on both populations; a pollen vector is required
known_source_native_structure.breeding_system_index: self/outcross seed-set ISI is similar (0.60 versus 0.63; P=0.77)
known_source_native_structure.realized_reproduction: Mona open fruit set is pollen limited relative to supplemental outcross and source-native multiplicative fitness for open/outcross progeny is lower than Guánica

primary_mapping.V_k: visit rate for visitor k on a common observation-effort / open-flower denominator
primary_mapping.E_k: source-native or newly measured per-visit effectiveness for visitor k, such as single-visit conspecific pollen deposition or another predeclared direct service outcome
forbidden_substitutes: transported effectiveness from another species or unmatched population

service_equivalence_identity.general_form: If one visitor aggregate dominates each population, equal total effective service requires E_Mona / E_Guanica = V_Guanica / V_Mona.
service_equivalence_identity.source_report_context: The primary source reports mean visitation in Guánica at approximately twice Mona; therefore exact service equivalence would require approximately twice the mean per-visit effectiveness on Mona only under the simplifying single-aggregate comparison.
service_equivalence_identity.boundary: The approximate factor of two is a descriptive consequence of the reported visitation contrast, not a recovered per-visit-effectiveness estimate and not an assumption allowed in primary inference. The full visitor-specific sum is preferred.

predeclared_interpretations.network_context_explains_most_realized_d: The measured difference in total effective service tracks the Guánica–Mona realized reproductive-performance contrast and leaves little unexplained sign discrepancy.
predeclared_interpretations.service_redundancy_detected: Despite lower or redistributed visitation, Mona total effective service is maintained because visitor-specific E_k compensates; this would be a network-context service-rescue observation but would conflict with calling whole reproductive performance buffered if realized output remains lower.
predeclared_interpretations.downstream_limit_after_service: Total effective service is similar but realized reproduction remains lower on Mona, implying a post-service reproductive/demographic limitation rather than service shortage alone.
predeclared_interpretations.service_limitation: Total effective service is lower on Mona and realized reproduction is lower in the same direction, supporting propagation through service limitation.
predeclared_interpretations.unresolved: Visitor-specific E_k or matched effort denominators remain missing.

required_new_data: matched visitor-specific visit rate by population
visitor-specific direct per-visit effectiveness on the same focal plant
matched reproductive outcome and supplemental-outcross capacity denominator when available

mapping_to_abm.reason: The empirical support/service variable is defined prospectively, but visitor-specific E_k values are not yet recovered/measured and no ABM state-value derivation rule has been frozen from source-native units.

claim_boundary: This preflight turns Guaiacum into a falsifiable service-mapping reference. It does not restore Guaiacum to the buffer portfolio, infer an Apis effect, or estimate missing effectiveness values.
